blocks.text:
# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

## PR Description

Closes #1600
### Root Cause
- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` (`build-mobile.yml`) + `build-macos` pinned the generic `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, which the repo's **Linux** self-hosted box also advertises → `Build iOS IPA` ran there with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127 at *Install fastlane*, run 38516656653).
- `bench-harbor.yml` wrote harbor output inside the shared workspace (`-o jobs` → docker-held `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` checkout failed before any build step.

### Previous Attempt
- Round-1 WIP (`ede8c5f3`, dev run 38734867908) factored the checkout into composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` via `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` at step time, which on the persistent box is the PREVIOUS run's tree: missing (first run) or stale (later), since the checkout IS what materializes it. Its single-quoted `preserve-cache-dir` also kept `$HOME` literal. Action deleted; logic inlined.

### Fix
- `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`: `build-ios`, `submit-ios`, `build-macos` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — fa-m5-1's unique registration label (gh-1005 convention from `ci.yml`).
- `bench-harbor.yml`: output moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (uploads follow); new `always()` step tears shard docker containers down before removing the output dir.
- All three mirror-checkout scripts hardened **inline**: log-and-prune clean (unremovable leftovers tolerated, remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, clone-around-stub last resort); build-macos cache park/restore best-effort.

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests, RED on `origin/main`, GREEN here: `macos-m5` pins + no-self-hosted-job-without-pin audit, out-of-workspace bench output, docker-teardown-before-rm (+ own `ENV_TYPE` scope), inline log-and-prune scripts, `$HOME`-expanded cache park order.
- Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (clean clone / cache park+restore / surviving-stub clone-around) — all pass; `bash -n` + YAML parse clean.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **10996 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped — host-dependent live legs), fresh run against the final tree.

### Notes
- Out of scope: CLI-leg `fa-extension.zip` size budget (+5.0% gate) — tracked class **#1262**.
- AC3 (next scheduled `daily-publish` green) verifies post-merge on the runner.

**Summary**: The `macos-m5` routing pin (AC1) and the out-of-workspace bench output + tolerant inline checkouts are correct and well-tested (10/10 static REGs green, checkout logic behaviorally verified). **Next Steps**:

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the docker teardown filter can never match — the cleanup step is a no-op**

`docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` filters by **container name**, but harbor 0.23.0 (the version pinned in this workflow's install step: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`) never puts the job name in container names. Verified from the harbor 0.23.0 wheel:

- `harbor/models/trial/config.py` — `generate_trial_name()` = `{task_name[:32]}__{ShortUUID(7)}` (task name + **random** suffix; `--job-name` only names the output dir `jobs_dir/job_name`)
- `harbor/trial/trial.py:1225` — environment `session_id = f"{self.config.trial_name}__env"`
- `harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:1380` — containers run under compose `--project-name _sanitize_docker_compose_project_name(session_id)` → container names look like `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`

So `docker rm -f $ids` never receives an id: a cancelled/interrupted shard still leaks its trial containers, they keep running (CPU/RAM on the persistent box) and keep holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` — the `rm -rf` below then only emits the warning. Ticket F-B's "post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm" and the PR description's "tears shard docker containers down" are not actually delivered, and the REG test greenlights a mechanism that cannot work. (Note: a naive "fix" that anchors the job-name filter would still match nothing — and if names ever DID carry the job name, the unanchored substring would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`.)

Fix: key on compose labels instead of names — every harbor trial container carries `com.docker.compose.project.*` labels:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*) docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
done
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: stub collision keeps the STALE leftover and deletes the FRESH entry**

In the clone-around-stub path, when a surviving stub collides with a repo path, the fresh entry is skipped ("left in $CLONE_TARGET") and then **deleted** by the trailing `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` — the workspace silently keeps the stale leftover at that path (warning-only). Today the realistic leftovers (`jobs/<run-id>/`) are not repo paths, so exposure is low, but the inversion is cheap and makes fresh content always win:


**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: prune old `stale-workspace-*` dirs before creating a new one**

The move-aside path parks an unremovable stale tree in `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-<ts>/`.         run: |

# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

## PR Description

Closes #1600
### Root Cause
- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` (`build-mobile.yml`) + `build-macos` pinned the generic `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, which the repo's **Linux** self-hosted box also advertises → `Build iOS IPA` ran there with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127 at *Install fastlane*, run 38516656653).
- `bench-harbor.yml` wrote harbor output inside the shared workspace (`-o jobs` → docker-held `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` checkout failed before any build step.

### Previous Attempt
- Round-1 WIP (`ede8c5f3`, dev run 38734867908) factored the checkout into composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` via `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` at step time, which on the persistent box is the PREVIOUS run's tree: missing (first run) or stale (later), since the checkout IS what materializes it. Its single-quoted `preserve-cache-dir` also kept `$HOME` literal. Action deleted; logic inlined.

### Fix
- `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`: `build-ios`, `submit-ios`, `build-macos` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — fa-m5-1's unique registration label (gh-1005 convention from `ci.yml`).
- `bench-harbor.yml`: output moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (uploads follow); new `always()` step tears shard docker containers down before removing the output dir.
- All three mirror-checkout scripts hardened **inline**: log-and-prune clean (unremovable leftovers tolerated, remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, clone-around-stub last resort); build-macos cache park/restore best-effort.

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests, RED on `origin/main`, GREEN here: `macos-m5` pins + no-self-hosted-job-without-pin audit, out-of-workspace bench output, docker-teardown-before-rm (+ own `ENV_TYPE` scope), inline log-and-prune scripts, `$HOME`-expanded cache park order.
- Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (clean clone / cache park+restore / surviving-stub clone-around) — all pass; `bash -n` + YAML parse clean.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **10996 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped — host-dependent live legs), fresh run against the final tree.

### Notes
- Out of scope: CLI-leg `fa-extension.zip` size budget (+5.0% gate) — tracked class **#1262**.
- AC3 (next scheduled `daily-publish` green) verifies post-merge on the runner.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the docker teardown filter can never match — the cleanup step is a no-op**

`docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` filters by **container name**, but harbor 0.23.0 (the version pinned in this workflow's install step: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`) never puts the job name in container names. Verified from the harbor 0.23.0 wheel:

- `harbor/models/trial/config.py` — `generate_trial_name()` = `{task_name[:32]}__{ShortUUID(7)}` (task name + **random** suffix; `--job-name` only names the output dir `jobs_dir/job_name`)
- `harbor/trial/trial.py:1225` — environment `session_id = f"{self.config.trial_name}__env"`
- `harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:1380` — containers run under compose `--project-name _sanitize_docker_compose_project_name(session_id)` → container names look like `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`

So `docker rm -f $ids` never receives an id: a cancelled/interrupted shard still leaks its trial containers, they keep running (CPU/RAM on the persistent box) and keep holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` — the `rm -rf` below then only emits the warning. Ticket F-B's "post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm" and the PR description's "tears shard docker containers down" are not actually delivered, and the REG test greenlights a mechanism that cannot work. (Note: a naive "fix" that anchors the job-name filter would still match nothing — and if names ever DID carry the job name, the unanchored substring would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`.)

Fix: key on compose labels instead of names — every harbor trial container carries `com.docker.compose.project.*` labels:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*) docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
done
```

(or match `com.docker.compose.project` names ending in `__env` with the working-dir check as the precision guard). Keep the teardown-before-`rm -rf` order and the best-effort error handling as written.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: stub collision keeps the STALE leftover and deletes the FRESH entry**

In the clone-around-stub path, when a surviving stub collides with a repo path, the fresh entry is skipped ("left in $CLONE_TARGET") and then **deleted** by the trailing `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` — the workspace silently keeps the stale leftover at that path (warning-only). Today the realistic leftovers (`jobs/<run-id>/`) are not repo paths, so exposure is low, but the inversion is cheap and makes fresh content always win:

```bash
if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$STALE" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE/" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
fi
```

(move the stub into the same `$STALE` sidecar; only fall back to skip-with-warning if even that `mv` fails). Applies to both `build-ios`/`submit-ios` and `build-macos` copies.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: prune old `stale-workspace-*` dirs before creating a new one**

The move-aside path parks an unremovable stale tree in `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-<ts>/`. On this persistent box the runner's own `_temp` cleanup cannot remove mount-held content either, so every degraded checkout leaves another timestamped dir behind — unbounded growth until manual cleanup. Cheap bound: best-effort prune of previous sidecars at the start of the same block (the containers that held them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds):

```bash
rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
```

Same one-liner applies to the `build-macos.yml` copy.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: extend the label audit to all workflows, not just the two publish legs**

This test (and the fix) covers `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` only. The routing-bug class dies properly if the audit asserts repo-wide: no workflow under `.github/workflows/` carries the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels at all. That assert is precise today — the only legitimate self-hosted legs left are `bench-mls.yml`'s bare `self-hosted` (the Linux box, correctly label-free of macOS) and `ci.yml`'s `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` — so a future `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` pin added anywhere (e.g. a new leg in `daily-publish.yml` or `release-appstore.yml`) would fail CI instead of re-routing an iOS-shaped job onto Linux a year from now. A simple glob over `.github/workflows/*.yml` greping `runs-on:` lines for `macOS|ARM64` is enough; no per-job whitelist needed.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed — the teardown no longer filters by container name.

`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (cleanup step, `Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)`):

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
torn=0
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
      docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      torn=$((torn + 1))
      ;;
  esac
done
```

- Selection is by the `com.docker.compose.project` label every harbor 0.23.0 trial container carries; the `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` label is the precision guard, so only containers bound to this runner's `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` output are removed — sibling shards and unrelated containers are untouched (and no name-anchor hack that would over-match `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`).

if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): harbor 0.23.0 never puts the
            # job name in container names — the compose project is
            # `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`, so trial containers look like
            # `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`. A `name=` filter can never
            # match (and an anchored one would still over-match sibling
            # shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`). Key on the compose labels
            # every harbor trial container carries and precision-guard on
            # the project working dir: only containers whose compose
            # project lives under THIS shard's $RUNNER_TEMP/bench output
            # are torn down.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              case "$wd" in
                "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                  docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                  torn=$((torn + 1))
                  ;;
              esac
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

blocks.text:
# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

## PR Description

Closes #1600
### Root Cause
- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` (`build-mobile.yml`) + `build-macos` pinned the generic `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, which the repo's **Linux** self-hosted box also advertises → `Build iOS IPA` ran there with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127 at *Install fastlane*, run 38516656653).
- `bench-harbor.yml` wrote harbor output inside the shared workspace (`-o jobs` → docker-held `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` checkout failed before any build step.

### Previous Attempt
- Round-1 WIP (`ede8c5f3`, dev run 38734867908) factored the checkout into composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` via `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` at step time, which on the persistent box is the PREVIOUS run's tree: missing (first run) or stale (later), since the checkout IS what materializes it. Its single-quoted `preserve-cache-dir` also kept `$HOME` literal. Action deleted; logic inlined.

### Fix
- `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`: `build-ios`, `submit-ios`, `build-macos` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — fa-m5-1's unique registration label (gh-1005 convention from `ci.yml`).
- `bench-harbor.yml`: output moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (uploads follow); new `always()` step tears shard docker containers down before removing the output dir.
- All three mirror-checkout scripts hardened **inline**: log-and-prune clean (unremovable leftovers tolerated, remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, clone-around-stub last resort); build-macos cache park/restore best-effort.

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests, RED on `origin/main`, GREEN here: `macos-m5` pins + no-self-hosted-job-without-pin audit, out-of-workspace bench output, docker-teardown-before-rm (+ own `ENV_TYPE` scope), inline log-and-prune scripts, `$HOME`-expanded cache park order.
- Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (clean clone / cache park+restore / surviving-stub clone-around) — all pass; `bash -n` + YAML parse clean.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **10996 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped — host-dependent live legs), fresh run against the final tree.

### Notes
- Out of scope: CLI-leg `fa-extension.zip` size budget (+5.0% gate) — tracked class **#1262**.
- AC3 (next scheduled `daily-publish` green) verifies post-merge on the runner.

🚨 **BLOCKING: the docker teardown filter can never match — the cleanup step is a no-op**

`docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` filters by **container name**, but harbor 0.23.0 (the version pinned in this workflow's install step: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`) never puts the job name in container names. Verified from the harbor 0.23.0 wheel:

- `harbor/models/trial/config.py` — `generate_trial_name()` = `{task_name[:32]}__{ShortUUID(7)}` (task name + **random** suffix; `--job-name` only names the output dir `jobs_dir/job_name`)
- `harbor/trial/trial.py:1225` — environment `session_id = f"{self.config.trial_name}__env"`
- `harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:1380` — containers run under compose `--project-name _sanitize_docker_compose_project_name(session_id)` → container names look like `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`

So `docker rm -f $ids` never receives an id: a cancelled/interrupted shard still leaks its trial containers, they keep running (CPU/RAM on the persistent box) and keep holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` — the `rm -rf` below then only emits the warning. Ticket F-B's "post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm" and the PR description's "tears shard docker containers down" are not actually delivered, and the REG test greenlights a mechanism that cannot work. (Note: a naive "fix" that anchors the job-name filter would still match nothing — and if names ever DID carry the job name, the unanchored substring would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`.)

Fix: key on compose labels instead of names — every harbor trial container carries `com.docker.compose.project.*` labels:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
```

💡 **SUGGESTION: stub collision keeps the STALE leftover and deletes the FRESH entry**

In the clone-around-stub path, when a surviving stub collides with a repo path, the fresh entry is skipped ("left in $CLONE_TARGET") and then **deleted** by the trailing `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` — the workspace silently keeps the stale leftover at that path (warning-only). # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.

      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor

# Re: Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

All findings are addressed on head `4ce3b655` (the rework-consume head):

## 🚨 Blocking — docker teardown filter was a no-op (`bench-harbor.yml`)

Fixed. The cleanup step (`Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)`) no longer filters by container name — harbor 0.23.0 names trial containers `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env-main-1`, so `--filter "name=fa-…"` could never match (and an anchored name would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`). The teardown now keys on the compose labels every harbor trial container carries and precision-guards on the project working dir:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
torn=0
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
      docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      torn=$((torn + 1))
      ;;
  esac
done
```

- `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` under this shard's own `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` output is the precision guard — sibling shards and unrelated containers are untouched.
- Teardown-before-`rm -rf` order, `always()`, the step-scoped `ENV_TYPE` copy, and best-effort handling are unchanged.

## 💡 Suggestions — all three applied

1. **Stub-collision inversion** — in all three inline checkout scripts (`build-ios`/`submit-ios` in `build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos` in `build-macos.yml`) the stale stub now moves into the same `$STALE` sidecar and the **fresh** entry moves in; skip-with-warning remains only as the last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
2. **`stale-workspace-*` pre-prune** — each move-aside block best-effort-prunes previous sidecars (`rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-*`) **before** creating the new timestamped one, bounding `RUNNER_TEMP` growth on the persistent box.
3. **Repo-wide label audit** — `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` now globs every `.github/workflows/*.yml` and asserts no job's `runs-on` carries the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels (precise today: `bench-mls.yml` is bare `self-hosted`, the macOS pins are `[self-hosted, macos-m5]`, GitHub-hosted `macos-latest` doesn't match the case-sensitive check).

## Verification

- 13/13 tests in `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` (4 new REG tests + updated teardown REG), RED on review head `d1a60f78` (old `name=fa-` filter present, 8 tests), GREEN on `4ce3b655`.

- `bash -n` on extracted scripts clean; all three workflow YAMLs parse.

```bash
if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then

  mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE/" 2>/dev/null || true
```

if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): harbor 0.23.0 never puts the
            # job name in container names — the compose project is
            # `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`, so trial containers look like
            # `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`. A `name=` filter can never
            # match (and an anchored one would still over-match sibling
            # shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`). Key on the compose labels
            # every harbor trial container carries and precision-guard on
            # the project working dir: only containers whose compose
            # project lives under THIS shard's $RUNNER_TEMP/bench output
            # are torn down.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              case "$wd" in
                "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                  docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                  torn=$((torn + 1))
                  ;;
              esac
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of

      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a

done

## PR Description

Closes #1600
### Root Cause
- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` (`build-mobile.yml`) + `build-macos` pinned the generic `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, which the repo's **Linux** self-hosted box also advertises → `Build iOS IPA` ran there with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127 at *Install fastlane*, run 38516656653).
- `bench-harbor.yml` wrote harbor output inside the shared workspace (`-o jobs` → docker-held `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` checkout failed before any build step.

### Previous Attempt
- Round-1 WIP (`ede8c5f3`, dev run 38734867908) factored the checkout into composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` via `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` at step time, which on the persistent box is the PREVIOUS run's tree: missing (first run) or stale (later), since the checkout IS what materializes it. Its single-quoted `preserve-cache-dir` also kept `$HOME` literal. Action deleted; logic inlined.

### Fix
- `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`: `build-ios`, `submit-ios`, `build-macos` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — fa-m5-1's unique registration label (gh-1005 convention from `ci.yml`).
- `bench-harbor.yml`: output moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (uploads follow); new `always()` step tears shard docker containers down before removing the output dir.
- All three mirror-checkout scripts hardened **inline**: log-and-prune clean (unremovable leftovers tolerated, remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, clone-around-stub last resort); build-macos cache park/restore best-effort.

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests, RED on `origin/main`, GREEN here: `macos-m5` pins + no-self-hosted-job-without-pin audit, out-of-workspace bench output, docker-teardown-before-rm (+ own `ENV_TYPE` scope), inline log-and-prune scripts, `$HOME`-expanded cache park order.
- Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (clean clone / cache park+restore / surviving-stub clone-around) — all pass; `bash -n` + YAML parse clean.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **10996 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped — host-dependent live legs), fresh run against the final tree.

### Notes
- Out of scope: CLI-leg `fa-extension.zip` size budget (+5.0% gate) — tracked class **#1262**.
- AC3 (next scheduled `daily-publish` green) verifies post-merge on the runner.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the docker teardown filter can never match — the cleanup step is a no-op**

`docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` filters by **container name**, but harbor 0.23.0 (the version pinned in this workflow's install step: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`) never puts the job name in container names. Verified from the harbor 0.23.0 wheel:

- `harbor/models/trial/config.py` — `generate_trial_name()` = `{task_name[:32]}__{ShortUUID(7)}` (task name + **random** suffix; `--job-name` only names the output dir `jobs_dir/job_name`)
- `harbor/trial/trial.py:1225` — environment `session_id = f"{self.config.trial_name}__env"`
- `harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:1380` — containers run under compose `--project-name _sanitize_docker_compose_project_name(session_id)` → container names look like `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`

So `docker rm -f $ids` never receives an id: a cancelled/interrupted shard still leaks its trial containers, they keep running (CPU/RAM on the persistent box) and keep holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` — the `rm -rf` below then only emits the warning. Ticket F-B's "post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm" and the PR description's "tears shard docker containers down" are not actually delivered, and the REG test greenlights a mechanism that cannot work. (Note: a naive "fix" that anchors the job-name filter would still match nothing — and if names ever DID carry the job name, the unanchored substring would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`.)

Fix: key on compose labels instead of names — every harbor trial container carries `com.docker.compose.project.*` labels:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*) docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
done
```

(or match `com.docker.compose.project` names ending in `__env` with the working-dir check as the precision guard). Keep the teardown-before-`rm -rf` order and the best-effort error handling as written.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: stub collision keeps the STALE leftover and deletes the FRESH entry**

In the clone-around-stub path, when a surviving stub collides with a repo path, the fresh entry is skipped ("left in $CLONE_TARGET") and then **deleted** by the trailing `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` — the workspace silently keeps the stale leftover at that path (warning-only). Today the realistic leftovers (`jobs/<run-id>/`) are not repo paths, so exposure is low, but the inversion is cheap and makes fresh content always win:

```bash
if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$STALE" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE/" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
fi
```

(move the stub into the same `$STALE` sidecar; only fall back to skip-with-warning if even that `mv` fails). Applies to both `build-ios`/`submit-ios` and `build-macos` copies.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: prune old `stale-workspace-*` dirs before creating a new one**

The move-aside path parks an unremovable stale tree in `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-<ts>/`. On this persistent box the runner's own `_temp` cleanup cannot remove mount-held content either, so every degraded checkout leaves another timestamped dir behind — unbounded growth until manual cleanup. Cheap bound: best-effort prune of previous sidecars at the start of the same block (the containers that held them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds):

```bash
rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
```

Same one-liner applies to the `build-macos.yml` copy.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: extend the label audit to all workflows, not just the two publish legs**

This test (and the fix) covers `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` only. The routing-bug class dies properly if the audit asserts repo-wide: no workflow under `.github/workflows/` carries the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels at all. That assert is precise today — the only legitimate self-hosted legs left are `bench-mls.yml`'s bare `self-hosted` (the Linux box, correctly label-free of macOS) and `ci.yml`'s `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` — so a future `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` pin added anywhere (e.g. a new leg in `daily-publish.yml` or `release-appstore.yml`) would fail CI instead of re-routing an iOS-shaped job onto Linux a year from now. A simple glob over `.github/workflows/*.yml` greping `runs-on:` lines for `macOS|ARM64` is enough; no per-job whitelist needed.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed — the teardown no longer filters by container name.

`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (cleanup step, `Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)`):

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
torn=0
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
      docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      torn=$((torn + 1))
      ;;
  esac
done
```

- Selection is by the `com.docker.compose.project` label every harbor 0.23.0 trial container carries; the `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` label is the precision guard, so only containers bound to this runner's `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` output are removed — sibling shards and unrelated containers are untouched (and no name-anchor hack that would over-match `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`).

if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): harbor 0.23.0 never puts the
            # job name in container names — the compose project is
            # `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`, so trial containers look like
            # `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`. A `name=` filter can never
            # match (and an anchored one would still over-match sibling
            # shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`). Key on the compose labels
            # every harbor trial container carries and precision-guard on
            # the project working dir: only containers whose compose
            # project lives under THIS shard's $RUNNER_TEMP/bench output
            # are torn down.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              case "$wd" in
                "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                  docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                  torn=$((torn + 1))
                  ;;
              esac
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).

## PR Description

Closes #1600
### Root Cause
- `build-ios`/`submit-ios` (`build-mobile.yml`) + `build-macos` pinned the generic `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, which the repo's **Linux** self-hosted box also advertises → `Build iOS IPA` ran there with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127 at *Install fastlane*, run 38516656653).
- `bench-harbor.yml` wrote harbor output inside the shared workspace (`-o jobs` → docker-held `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` checkout failed before any build step.

### Previous Attempt
- Round-1 WIP (`ede8c5f3`, dev run 38734867908) factored the checkout into composite action `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` via `uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout` — a local `./` action resolves against `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` at step time, which on the persistent box is the PREVIOUS run's tree: missing (first run) or stale (later), since the checkout IS what materializes it. Its single-quoted `preserve-cache-dir` also kept `$HOME` literal. Action deleted; logic inlined.

### Fix
- `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`: `build-ios`, `submit-ios`, `build-macos` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — fa-m5-1's unique registration label (gh-1005 convention from `ci.yml`).
- `bench-harbor.yml`: output moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs` (uploads follow); new `always()` step tears shard docker containers down before removing the output dir.
- All three mirror-checkout scripts hardened **inline**: log-and-prune clean (unremovable leftovers tolerated, remainder moved to `$RUNNER_TEMP`, clone-around-stub last resort); build-macos cache park/restore best-effort.

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — 10 tests, RED on `origin/main`, GREEN here: `macos-m5` pins + no-self-hosted-job-without-pin audit, out-of-workspace bench output, docker-teardown-before-rm (+ own `ENV_TYPE` scope), inline log-and-prune scripts, `$HOME`-expanded cache park order.
- Behavioral sim of the exact committed checkout scripts (clean clone / cache park+restore / surviving-stub clone-around) — all pass; `bash -n` + YAML parse clean.
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **10996 passed, 0 failed** (10 skipped — host-dependent live legs), fresh run against the final tree.

### Notes
- Out of scope: CLI-leg `fa-extension.zip` size budget (+5.0% gate) — tracked class **#1262**.
- AC3 (next scheduled `daily-publish` green) verifies post-merge on the runner.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the docker teardown filter can never match — the cleanup step is a no-op**

`docker ps -aq --filter "name=fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${KIND}-${SHARD}"` filters by **container name**, but harbor 0.23.0 (the version pinned in this workflow's install step: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`) never puts the job name in container names. Verified from the harbor 0.23.0 wheel:

- `harbor/models/trial/config.py` — `generate_trial_name()` = `{task_name[:32]}__{ShortUUID(7)}` (task name + **random** suffix; `--job-name` only names the output dir `jobs_dir/job_name`)
- `harbor/trial/trial.py:1225` — environment `session_id = f"{self.config.trial_name}__env"`
- `harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:1380` — containers run under compose `--project-name _sanitize_docker_compose_project_name(session_id)` → container names look like `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`

So `docker rm -f $ids` never receives an id: a cancelled/interrupted shard still leaks its trial containers, they keep running (CPU/RAM on the persistent box) and keep holding `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` — the `rm -rf` below then only emits the warning. Ticket F-B's "post-run cleanup tears docker containers down before rm" and the PR description's "tears shard docker containers down" are not actually delivered, and the REG test greenlights a mechanism that cannot work. (Note: a naive "fix" that anchors the job-name filter would still match nothing — and if names ever DID carry the job name, the unanchored substring would over-match sibling shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`.)

Fix: key on compose labels instead of names — every harbor trial container carries `com.docker.compose.project.*` labels:

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*) docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
done
```

(or match `com.docker.compose.project` names ending in `__env` with the working-dir check as the precision guard). Keep the teardown-before-`rm -rf` order and the best-effort error handling as written.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: stub collision keeps the STALE leftover and deletes the FRESH entry**

In the clone-around-stub path, when a surviving stub collides with a repo path, the fresh entry is skipped ("left in $CLONE_TARGET") and then **deleted** by the trailing `rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"` — the workspace silently keeps the stale leftover at that path (warning-only). Today the realistic leftovers (`jobs/<run-id>/`) are not repo paths, so exposure is low, but the inversion is cheap and makes fresh content always win:

```bash
if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$STALE" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE/" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
fi
```

(move the stub into the same `$STALE` sidecar; only fall back to skip-with-warning if even that `mv` fails). Applies to both `build-ios`/`submit-ios` and `build-macos` copies.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: prune old `stale-workspace-*` dirs before creating a new one**

The move-aside path parks an unremovable stale tree in `$RUNNER_TEMP/stale-workspace-<ts>/`. On this persistent box the runner's own `_temp` cleanup cannot remove mount-held content either, so every degraded checkout leaves another timestamped dir behind — unbounded growth until manual cleanup. Cheap bound: best-effort prune of previous sidecars at the start of the same block (the containers that held them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds):

```bash
rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
```

Same one-liner applies to the `build-macos.yml` copy.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

💡 **SUGGESTION: extend the label audit to all workflows, not just the two publish legs**

This test (and the fix) covers `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` only. The routing-bug class dies properly if the audit asserts repo-wide: no workflow under `.github/workflows/` carries the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels at all. That assert is precise today — the only legitimate self-hosted legs left are `bench-mls.yml`'s bare `self-hosted` (the Linux box, correctly label-free of macOS) and `ci.yml`'s `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` — so a future `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` pin added anywhere (e.g. a new leg in `daily-publish.yml` or `release-appstore.yml`) would fail CI instead of re-routing an iOS-shaped job onto Linux a year from now. A simple glob over `.github/workflows/*.yml` greping `runs-on:` lines for `macOS|ARM64` is enough; no per-job whitelist needed.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):

Fixed — the teardown no longer filters by container name.

`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (cleanup step, `Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)`):

```bash
ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
torn=0
for c in $ids; do
  wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$wd" in
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
      docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      torn=$((torn + 1))
      ;;
  esac
done
```

- Selection is by the `com.docker.compose.project` label every harbor 0.23.0 trial container carries; the `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir` label is the precision guard, so only containers bound to this runner's `$RUNNER_TEMP/bench` output are removed — sibling shards and unrelated containers are untouched (and no name-anchor hack that would over-match `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`).

if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): harbor 0.23.0 never puts the
            # job name in container names — the compose project is
            # `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`, so trial containers look like
            # `some-task__ab12cd3__env-main-1`. A `name=` filter can never
            # match (and an anchored one would still over-match sibling
            # shards, `…-cpu-1` ⊂ `…-cpu-14`). Key on the compose labels
            # every harbor trial container carries and precision-guard on
            # the project working dir: only containers whose compose
            # project lives under THIS shard's $RUNNER_TEMP/bench output
            # are torn down.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              wd=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              case "$wd" in
                "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench"/*)
                  docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                  torn=$((torn + 1))
                  ;;
              esac
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to $RUNNER_TEMP/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::$RUNNER_TEMP/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time, and on this box the workspace is the
      # PREVIOUS run's tree — the action file would be missing (first run) or
      # stale, since this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a
            # live bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build
            # the checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A
            # bench leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path;
            # if one ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"
          if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r entry; do
              name="$(basename "$entry")"
              if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
